titre: The Anthropocene doesn't exist, at least not officially
accroche: The word has been everywhere for twenty years. In March 2024, the geologists charged with deciding voted against its official adoption.
contenu_vulgarise:
The word “Anthropocene” has been circulating since the early 2000s to designate a new geological epoch, one in which human action would have become the dominant force shaping the planet. It has become part of public debate, to the point that one might think the question was settled. It is not.

## A procedure, a vote

Getting a name into the geological time scale is not a media decision: it is a formal procedure, conducted by the Subcommission on Quaternary Stratigraphy, a body of the International Commission on Stratigraphy, itself attached to the International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS). The Anthropocene Working Group, active since 2009, had proposed a precise reference site: a core of laminated lake sediments from Crawford Lake, in Ontario, where a spike of radionuclides from nuclear testing would mark, around 1952, the official start of the new epoch.

The ballot opened on February 1, 2024, and closed on March 4. The result: 4 votes in favor, 12 against, 3 abstentions. The Commission's executive committee recognized the vote as valid, and the chairs of the Commission's seventeen subcommissions supported that recognition: 15 in favor, 1 abstention, 1 conflict of interest. The Union announced it in a press release dated March 20, 2024. The Anthropocene did not become a formal geological epoch.

## What the critics objected to

The Union's extended press release reports the objections of the proposal's critics. They do not concern the reality of human influence, but the form it was meant to be given. The effects of the human species on climate and landscapes long predate the mid-20th century: early agriculture, the Industrial Revolution in Western Europe, and the colonization of the Americas already bear their mark. A unit shorter than a human lifetime sits awkwardly in a scale where each unit spans thousands or even millions of years. Finally, human effects vary by region and by era, so their onset cannot be represented by a single, simultaneous horizon. The press release adds that many members of the subcommission were unconvinced by the arguments in the proposal.

The same text describes an alternative narrative: treating the Anthropocene not as an epoch but as an “event,” like the Great Oxygenation, the Cambrian Explosion, or the Great Ordovician Biodiversification. None of these events is a chronostratigraphic unit, so none has required formal ratification.

## What the rejection doesn't change

The official press release itself specifies it: the word will continue to be widely used, by the Earth sciences as well as by the social sciences, policymakers, or the general public. What the vote closes is only its status as an official chronostratigraphic unit, the precise slot that the Holocene, the Pleistocene, or the Jurassic each fill. Officially, we are still in the Holocene, and more precisely in its most recent age, the Meghalayan.

repere.texte: The vote of the Subcommission on Quaternary Stratigraphy, closed on March 4, 2024, rejected the proposal by 12 votes to 4 (3 abstentions). Crawford Lake (Ontario, Canada) was the candidate site to mark, around 1950, the official start of the Anthropocene.
repere.source: IUGS / ICS, press release of March 20, 2024

carte.punch: The Anthropocene has never been officially adopted as a geological epoch.
carte.idee: The word has been circulating for twenty years, but never as an official geological epoch. In March 2024, the body charged with deciding voted against it, by 12 votes to 4 (3 abstentions). Critics judged human influence too old and too diffuse for a single dated marker.

quiz.question: What fundamental objection did critics of the proposal raise, according to the Union's press release?
choix: The traces of human influence in the sediments of Crawford Lake were insufficient
Human impact on the planet is not established
The vote had not gathered enough voters to be valid
Human influence is older and more diffuse than a single dated marker assumes
quiz.explication: The critics do not question the reality of human impact, but the form proposed: a single instant around 1950 fits poorly with a phenomenon that began well before and whose intensity varies by region. The vote was recognized as valid by the Commission's executive committee.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What was the result of the ballot closed on March 4, 2024?
choix: 4 votes in favor, 12 against, and 3 abstentions
12 votes in favor, 4 against, and 3 abstentions
A majority in favor, later overturned by the executive committee
A tie, for lack of a quorum
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The vote of the Subcommission on Quaternary Stratigraphy, opened on February 1 and closed on March 4, 2024, gave 4 votes in favor, 12 against, and 3 abstentions. The Commission's executive committee recognized the vote as valid; the Union announced it in its press release of March 20.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which site had been proposed to mark the start of the Anthropocene?
choix: A Greenland peat bog, dated to the Industrial Revolution
A sediment core from Crawford Lake, in Ontario
An Australian coral reef marked by bleaching
A fossilized plastic layer on a beach in Bermuda
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The working group proposed the laminated lake sediments of Crawford Lake, in Ontario, where a spike of radionuclides from nuclear testing would mark, around the middle of the 20th century, the start of the new epoch.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In which unit of the time scale are we officially?
choix: In the Anthropocene, provisionally adopted in 2024
In the Pleistocene, which was never closed
In the Holocene, and in its most recent age, the Meghalayan
In none, the vote having suspended the official scale
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The rejection leaves the scale unchanged: we remain in the Holocene, and more precisely in the Meghalayan, its most recent age. The word Anthropocene continues to be used, but without official chronostratigraphic status.
